title: Sonny and the Little Quoll | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka spots a shy spotted quoll hiding behind a log in the moonlight, and by sitting very still and waiting patiently, she makes the shyest little friend in the whole bush. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
Two eyes in the dark.

Sunny almost didn't see them — just a pair of bright, careful eyes watching her from behind a mossy log at the edge of the path.

She stopped. She kept very still.

Slowly, she made herself as quiet and small as she could.

The eyes watched her.

She waited.

A nose appeared — a small pointed nose, twitching.

Then the whole face — and what a face. Enormous dark eyes, small round ears, a pointed muzzle. And its body, when it finally crept forward on cautious silent paws, was dotted all over with small white spots — like a scattering of stars on dark brown velvet.

A quoll. A very small, very shy quoll.

Sunny did not reach for it. She did not make a sound. She simply stayed exactly where she was, as still as the moss and the rocks around her.

The quoll crept a little closer. Then stopped. Its nose twitched again.

Then, very slowly, it moved until it was just an arm's length away, and it curled up behind the other side of the log — close, but safe.

Sunny felt her heart do something warm.

They stayed like that — Sunny on one side of the log, the little quoll on the other — sharing the moonlit quiet.

And one by one, they both went to sleep.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, little quoll. Goodnight, little one.
